\section[la antigüedad]{la antigüedad — antiquity, the ancient world; age}

\label{lesson:ES-C575-antiguedad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the television news, then the Spanish for the incident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la antigüedad}
\textbf{la antigüedad} — \textquotedblleft{}antiquity, the ancient world; age\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
En la Antigüedad no había relojes como los de hoy.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In ancient times there were no clocks like today's.}
\end{quote}

At work it means seniority: \emph{años de antigüedad}. \emph{Una tienda de antigüedades} sells antiques.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{antigüedad} comes from Latin \emph{antīquitās}, \emph{antīquitātem} 'age, antiquity' (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{antīquus} 'old'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la antigüedad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la antigüedad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la antigüedad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the television news, then the Spanish for the incident, then say \emph{la antigüedad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la antigüedad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Antiquity, the ancient world; age\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el presente]{el presente — the present}

\label{lesson:ES-C575-presente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the incident, then the Spanish for antiquity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el presente}
\textbf{el presente} — \textquotedblleft{}the present\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay que vivir el presente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You have to live in the present.}
\end{quote}

As an adjective it means present: \emph{Estaba presente.} In class, \emph{¡Presente!} — here!

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{presente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praesēns} 'at hand, present' (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{prae} 'before' and the verb \emph{esse} 'to be'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el presente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el presente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el presente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the incident, then the Spanish for antiquity, then say \emph{el presente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el presente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The present\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el porvenir]{el porvenir — the future (what lies ahead)}

\label{lesson:ES-C575-porvenir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for antiquity, then the Spanish for the present.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el porvenir}
\textbf{el porvenir} — \textquotedblleft{}the future (what lies ahead)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nadie sabe qué nos traerá el porvenir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nobody knows what the future will bring us.}
\end{quote}

A little literary; it often means someone's prospects: \emph{un joven con porvenir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{porvenir} is built on \emph{por} and \emph{venir} 'to come', which is inherited from Latin \emph{venīre} 'to come' (EtymDB). The future is what is still to come.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el porvenir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el porvenir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el porvenir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for antiquity, then the Spanish for the present, then say \emph{el porvenir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el porvenir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The future (what lies ahead)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[antiguo]{antiguo — old, ancient; former}

\label{lesson:ES-C575-antiguo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the present, then the Spanish for the future.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: antiguo}
\textbf{antiguo} — \textquotedblleft{}old, ancient; former\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vivimos en un edificio muy antiguo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We live in a very old building.}
\end{quote}

Before a noun it can mean former: \emph{mi antiguo jefe} — my old boss.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{antiguo} is inherited from Latin \emph{antīquus} 'old, of former times' (EtymDB), through old Spanish \emph{antigo}; it is built on \emph{ante} 'before'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antiguo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antiguo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{antiguo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the present, then the Spanish for the future, then say \emph{antiguo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does antiguo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Old, ancient; former\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[antiguamente]{antiguamente — in the old days, formerly}

\label{lesson:ES-C575-antiguamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the future, then the Spanish for old.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: antiguamente}
\textbf{antiguamente} — \textquotedblleft{}in the old days, formerly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Antiguamente la gente viajaba a caballo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the old days people travelled on horseback.}
\end{quote}

Usually with the imperfect: \emph{Antiguamente aquí había un río.}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{antiguamente} is built on \emph{antiguo} and the ending \emph{-mente}, from Latin \emph{mente} 'with a mind'. \emph{Antiguo} comes from Latin \emph{antīquus} 'of former times' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antiguamente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antiguamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{antiguamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the future, then the Spanish for old, then say \emph{antiguamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does antiguamente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In the old days, formerly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Más sucesos y relatos}

\label{lesson:ES-R575-repaso-568-575}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for historic and the revolution.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item historic, the revolution, the monarch, the queen, to conquer
  \item to fight, to defeat, to beat, to defend, the conflict
  \item the demonstration, the protest, the disturbance, the scandal, the controversy
  \item the inventor, the discovery, the invention, the origin, the development
  \item to become, to transform, to evolve, to develop, to overcome
  \item to reach, to fail, the failure, to suffer, to turn out
  \item to hear about, to receive, the notification, the television news, the incident
  \item antiquity, the present, the future, old, in the old days
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Historic? (\textbf{histórico}.) The revolution? (\textbf{la revolución}.) The monarch? (\textbf{el monarca}.) The queen? (\textbf{la reina}.) To conquer? (\textbf{conquistar}.) To fight? (\textbf{luchar}.) To defeat? (\textbf{derrotar}.) To beat? (\textbf{vencer}.) To defend? (\textbf{defender}.) The conflict? (\textbf{el conflicto}.) The demonstration? (\textbf{la manifestación}.) The protest? (\textbf{la protesta}.) The disturbance? (\textbf{el disturbio}.) The scandal? (\textbf{el escándalo}.) The controversy? (\textbf{la polémica}.) The inventor? (\textbf{el inventor}.) The discovery? (\textbf{el descubrimiento}.) The invention? (\textbf{el invento}.) The origin? (\textbf{el origen}.) The development? (\textbf{el desarrollo}.) To become? (\textbf{convertirse}.) To transform? (\textbf{transformar}.) To evolve? (\textbf{evolucionar}.) To develop? (\textbf{desarrollar}.) To overcome? (\textbf{superar}.) To reach? (\textbf{alcanzar}.) To fail? (\textbf{fracasar}.) The failure? (\textbf{el fracaso}.) To suffer? (\textbf{sufrir}.) To turn out? (\textbf{resultar}.) To hear about? (\textbf{enterarse}.) To receive? (\textbf{recibir}.) The notification? (\textbf{la notificación}.) The television news? (\textbf{el telediario}.) The incident? (\textbf{el incidente}.) Antiquity? (\textbf{la antigüedad}.) The present? (\textbf{el presente}.) The future? (\textbf{el porvenir}.) Old? (\textbf{antiguo}.) In the old days? (\textbf{antiguamente}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
